title: The Supplier Returns Counted on a Travel Protection Plans Certificate
content:
Which of a supplier's returns count as the amount the supplier has paid the traveller, when a restoration is rated against a Travel Protection Plans certificate, is decided from the traveller's air booking sold under the Air Ticket Fare Brands: the notices of the airline's own disruption posted to that booking, the standing of the booking, and the lines the airline has returned on it. The quantity so scoped is taken as a positive amount.

Where the traveller's booking carries a notice of the supplier's own disruption and the booking stands as travelled, the amount the supplier has paid is taken as the amounts the supplier raised on that disruption alone.

Where the traveller's booking carries a notice of the supplier's own disruption and the booking does not stand as travelled, the amount the supplier has paid is taken as the amounts the supplier has returned on the booking in the six months to the declaration.

Where neither holds, the amount the supplier has paid is taken as every amount the supplier has returned on the traveller's booking for the journey.

## The three scopes

| Notices of the supplier's own disruption on the booking | Standing of the booking | The amount the supplier has paid is taken as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| At least 1 stands | The booking stands as travelled | The amounts the supplier raised on that disruption alone |
| At least 1 stands | The booking does not stand as travelled | The amounts the supplier has returned on the booking in the 6 months to the declaration |
| None stands | Any standing | Every amount the supplier has returned on the traveller's booking for the journey |

## Reading the booking

Both of the first two scopes require a notice of the supplier's own disruption to stand on the booking; they are told apart by the standing of the booking alone. Where the booking stands as travelled, only what the airline raised on that disruption is counted, and returns of other kinds are left out. Where it stands as anything else, every return on the booking is counted, but only those falling in the six months up to the day of the declaration.

Where no such notice stands on the booking, neither of those narrowings is reached, and the whole of what the airline has returned on the booking for the journey is counted, whatever its date and whatever the booking's standing.

Hypothetically, on a booking carrying one disruption notice and standing as travelled, returns of 400.00 USD raised on that disruption and 250.00 USD raised on other grounds give an amount the supplier has paid of 400.00 USD. On the same booking standing otherwise than as travelled, with 400.00 USD returned eight months ago and 250.00 USD returned last month, the amount the supplier has paid is 250.00 USD.
